answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity stake bond plus earned history. A new agent must post collateral in a scarce external asset before it can earn or vote, and the bond is slashed on proven fraud. A thousand fake agents cost a thousand full deposits, so the swarm's price rises linearly while its payoff does not; an honest operator risks one bond on real work. Signed receipts add a second lock: honest agents inherit trust from past jobs, while fresh identities start at zero. A forged identity is an onyx with no lantern behind it, alone on a cold ledge until it pays in full.
